text: Hands under shoulders, knees under hips, spine long.

review.notes: Convention for setup; Stevens studied four-point kneeling lifts.

text: Reach long, keeping hips and shoulders level.

review.notes: Level pelvis is convention; Stevens and Callaghan support single-leg and arm-and-leg lifts as low-load trunk work.

text: Pause a second, belly lightly braced, back steady.

review.notes: Kavcic ranks stabilisation exercises by spine stability and load; the bracing wording and hold time are convention.

text: Return slowly; do not let your back sag.

review.notes: Callaghan says holding the spine still while a limb moves is low-risk; the sag cue is convention.

text: Lie on your back, knees over hips, arms up.

review.notes: Convention. McGill 1998 covers trunk-stability principles generally, not this exact position.

text: Keep your lower back gently resting on the floor.

review.notes: Convention. No source found that tests the flat-back cue in the dead bug.

text: Lower opposite arm and leg slowly, only as far as you control.

review.notes: Convention; limits the range to what the trunk can control.

text: Breathe out as you lower; do not hold your breath.

review.notes: Convention. Breath holding tends to tense the neck; not tested here.

text: Elbows under shoulders, forearms flat, body in one line.

review.notes: Ekstrom studied the prone bridge on elbows and toes; the elbow position wording is convention.

text: Gently squeeze glutes and belly; keep hips level.

review.notes: Okubo measured deep abdominal activity in elbow-toe planks; the glute cue is convention.

text: Look at the floor, neck long and relaxed.

review.notes: Convention. No source found on neck position in the plank.

text: Keep breathing steadily; stop when your form slips.

review.notes: Convention. Ending a hold when form drops is common coaching; not tested here.

text: Elbow under shoulder, feet stacked or one in front.

review.notes: Youdas used side-bridge variations; foot position and the wording are convention.

text: Lift hips until shoulders, hips and knees line up.

review.notes: Ekstrom tested the side bridge; the straight-line wording is convention.

text: Push the floor away; keep your shoulder from your ear.

review.notes: Convention for shoulder position. Shoulder load is not measured in the source.

text: Breathe steadily; lower if your hips start to drop.

review.notes: Convention. McGill 1998 discusses trunk exercise in general; the stopping rule is ours.

text: Lie face down, forehead toward the floor, neck long.

review.notes: Convention. Callaghan studied extensor exercises but this exact setup is not described in the abstract.

text: Lift arms and legs only a few centimetres.

review.notes: Callaghan found active trunk extension gives the highest spine load, so a small lift is a convention-based safety limit.

text: Pause, squeeze glutes, then lower slowly.

review.notes: Convention.

text: Hands under shoulders, knees under hips, relaxed neck.

review.notes: Convention. McGill describes cat-camel as a spine mobility movement; confirm in full text.

text: Stay in a comfortable range; stop if it sharply hurts.

review.notes: Convention and safety wording; no pain-relief claim.

text: Breathe out as you round, in as you arch.

review.notes: Convention. Breathing pairing is common coaching, not tested.

text: Let your head follow your spine; keep your neck long.

review.notes: Convention.

text: Feet hip-width apart, band at chest height, stand sideways.

review.notes: Juan-Recio studied the Pallof press as a lumbopelvic control task; setup details are convention.

text: Press straight out; do not let the band turn you.

review.notes: Resisting rotation is the point of the exercise; wording is ours.

text: Hold one second, ribs down, hips square.

review.notes: Hold time and rib cue are convention.

text: Bring your hands back to your chest slowly.

review.notes: Convention.

text: Lie back, one knee bent, other leg straight.

review.notes: Felicio studied straight leg raises; setup wording is convention.

text: Tighten the thigh first, then lift the straight leg.

review.notes: Felicio supports quadriceps activity in this exercise; the tighten-first cue is convention.

text: Lift to the height of your bent knee, then pause.

review.notes: Convention for the stopping height.

text: Lower slowly; keep your lower back from arching.

review.notes: Convention.

text: Pick a clear, flat path with something to hold nearby.

review.notes: Ansari tested treadmill walking; path and support advice is safety convention.

text: Take short steps, reach back toe first, then heel.

review.notes: Convention for step style.

text: Glance behind often; stop if you feel unsteady.

review.notes: Safety convention.

text: Stand tall, eyes ahead, no leaning.

review.notes: Ansari found back muscles work harder in backward walking; the posture cue is convention.

text: Arms straight at chest height, hands shoulder-width apart.

review.notes: Fukunaga tested pull-apart hand positions; wording is ours.

text: Pull the band apart, squeezing shoulder blades together.

review.notes: Fukunaga shows shoulder-blade muscle activity; the squeeze cue is convention.

text: Ribs down; do not lean back.

review.notes: Convention. Trunk posture not studied in the paper.

text: Keep your shoulders away from your ears, neck relaxed.

review.notes: Convention. Upper trapezius activity was measured but not the shrug cue.
